theme: Late-summer harvest: two big building blocks — a roasted tomato sugo and a pot of brothy cannellini — that carry a full-house week (2 adults + 4 girls).

components.name: Roasted Summer Tomato Sugo
components.ingredients: 3 lb ripe summer tomatoes + two 28-oz cans San Marzano, 1 head garlic, 2 onions, 1 red pepper, generous olive oil, basil, salt
components.method: Halve fresh tomatoes and pepper, scatter with sliced onion and smashed garlic on two sheet pans, drown in olive oil and salt, roast at 425F for 45 min until charred and collapsed. Scrape everything (juices too) into a pot with the crushed canned tomatoes, simmer 20-25 min, then hit with a stick blender for a few pulses so it stays rustic. Stir in torn basil off the heat. Makes ~8 cups — enough for three dinners with a container to freeze.

components.name: Brothy Cannellini Beans
components.ingredients: 1 lb dried cannellini (soaked overnight), 6 garlic cloves, a few sage leaves, 1 halved onion, olive oil, salt, parmesan rind if you have one
components.method: Drain the soaked beans into a heavy pot, cover by two inches with fresh water, add garlic, sage, onion, parmesan rind and a long glug of olive oil. Bring to a bare simmer and cook 60-80 min until creamy but intact — salt only in the last 20 min. Let them cool in their own broth (this is your best kid-friendly bean liquid). Keep beans IN the liquid; makes ~6 cups.

dinners.name: Rigatoni al Forno
dinners.ingredients: 1.5 lb rigatoni, 4 cups sugo, 12 oz fresh mozzarella, parmesan, basil
steps: Boil rigatoni 2 min shy of al dente, drain.
Toss pasta with 4 cups sugo and half the torn mozzarella in a big baking dish.
Top with the rest of the mozzarella and a heavy shower of parmesan.
Bake at 425F for 18-20 min until bubbling and browned; rest 5 min before serving. The crowd-pleaser for the girls.

dinners.name: Pan-Seared Cod over Beans & Greens
dinners.ingredients: 4-6 cod or hake fillets, 3 cups cannellini + broth, 1 bunch escarole or spinach, garlic, lemon, olive oil
steps: Warm beans with a ladle of their broth and a splash of olive oil; wilt in chopped greens and a smashed garlic clove.
Pat cod dry, salt well, sear in a hot olive-oiled pan 3-4 min per side until golden.
Spoon beans and greens into bowls, set cod on top, finish with lemon and raw olive oil.
For the girls: serve their cod plain with beans on the side, greens optional.

dinners.name: Skillet Spaghetti al Pomodoro
dinners.ingredients: 1.25 lb spaghetti, 3 cups sugo, butter, parmesan, basil, reserved pasta water
steps: Boil spaghetti in well-salted water; pull it a minute early and save a mug of pasta water.
Warm sugo in a wide skillet, drop the pasta straight in with a splash of pasta water.
Toss hard over the heat with a knob of butter and a fistful of parmesan until the sauce turns glossy and clings — that's the mantecatura.
Finish with basil and olive oil; the kids get theirs first, less garlicky.

dinners.name: White Bean & Tomato Minestra
dinners.ingredients: 2 cups sugo, 2 cups beans + broth, small pasta or ditalini, 1 zucchini, carrot, parmesan rind, olive oil
steps: Sweat diced carrot and zucchini in olive oil until soft.
Add sugo, beans with their broth, a parmesan rind and enough water for a brothy soup; simmer 15 min.
Stir in a handful of small pasta and cook until tender.
Ladle out, top with parmesan and raw olive oil — mild and cozy for a full table.

technique.name: Mantecatura (finishing pasta in the pan)
technique.tiedTo: Skillet Spaghetti al Pomodoro — pull the pasta early, marry it to the sugo with pasta water, butter and parmesan, and toss vigorously off-heat so the starch emulsifies the sauce into a glossy coat instead of a puddle. This is the move that separates restaurant pasta from home pasta.

shopping.items: 3 lb ripe summer tomatoes, 1 red pepper, 3 onions, 2 heads garlic, 1 bunch escarole or spinach, 1 zucchini, 1 carrot, fresh basil, sage, lemons
4-6 cod or hake fillets (about 2 lb for the full house)
12 oz fresh mozzarella, wedge of parmesan (plus a rind if available), butter
1 lb dried cannellini, two 28-oz cans San Marzano tomatoes, 1.5 lb rigatoni, 1.25 lb spaghetti, small pasta/ditalini, good olive oil, salt

scaleNote: This is a FULL-HOUSE week (2 adults + 4 girls under 10, 6 at the table). Quantities above already serve 6 — keep the sugo and bean batches as written since both dinners lean on them heavily. For the girls: serve the rigatoni and the mild minestra as-is, plate their cod plain with beans on the side, and give them the skillet pasta before you add extra garlic or chili. If it's ever just you and Mike, halve the fresh pasta and fish but still make the full component batches — you'll want the leftover sugo and beans for lunches and the freezer.
